solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Big and beautiful!

definitions.meaning: a ... sum or profit is a big one

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising something both large and lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a generous, sizeable amount, and attractive in looks.

clue.text: Very able recruits initially residing in tough US university

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so the picked letters sit within the other word
initially signals taking the opening letter of each of the three preceding words

explanation.surface: Elite students being recruited to a demanding American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard is the oldest Ivy League institution of higher learning, in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

clue.text: Same novel under new titles

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the rearranged letters below the abbreviation for new
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of the word before it are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A book reissued unchanged but with new titles on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges SAME into AMES, which 'under' places beneath N.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles are what things are called, a synonym in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Player heading for success prospers: not bad!

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A competitor who heads for victory and does well: not a bad result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' here means an athlete, not a musician or actor; the colon is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in a game is an athlete or competitor, a synonym.

clue.text: Papa's partner embracing good, hot rock

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Papa's partner is Mama, the mother

explanation.surface: Dad's other half, kind and attractive, hugging him.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten material beneath the earth's crust, literally a very hot form of stone.

clue.text: Religious education in the morning papers

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Pupils studying divinity first thing, perhaps with newspapers to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of sheets, 500 of them, so a bundle of paper.

clue.text: Obvious I had to enter competition

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the contraction sits within the contest word

parts.note: an event is a contest or competition
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone stating plainly that they had signed up for a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident and obvious are synonyms: plain to see.

clue.text: Strength — could be

definitions.meaning: the past of may, expressing possibility, as in it may well be

explanation.surface: A musing that strength might be the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means power; the modal verb expresses possibility.

clue.text: Blue square

definitions.meaning: blue is the colour of Britain's Tory party, so a Blue is one of its supporters
square means old-fashioned and traditional in outlook

explanation.surface: A colour paired with a shape, as in a children's sorting game.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the colour of Britain's Tory party; square means traditional, unadventurous.

clue.text: Great lover, antipodean native hugging me

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, is native to Australia

explanation.surface: A passionate suitor down under being embraced by a local.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, Shakespeare's lover of Juliet, is the byword for an ardent wooer.

clue.text: Increasing success in sailors' drink

indicators.note: in places the victory word inside the rum ration word

parts.note: grog is rum and water, the traditional naval ration

explanation.surface: More and more victories credited to sailors' rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing and increasing are synonyms: getting bigger.

clue.text: Fool, a silly sausage for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first parts, so the opening letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Calling someone a silly sausage, an affectionate insult.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a stupid person, an idiot, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Passing trains, ten diverted

indicators.note: diverted means sent a different way, so the letters are rerouted into a new order

explanation.surface: Ten railway trains rerouted as they go by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' is the adjective sense, fleeting, not trains going past.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient lasts only briefly, a synonym for passing in the sense of fleeting.

clue.text: Somewhat shabby, poor design seen from the back is sagging

indicators.note: seen from the back means read from the end, so the run is read backwards
somewhat means only part of, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A building or garment, a bit tatty and badly designed, slumping when viewed from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The run Y POOR D, in 'shabby, poor design', read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy means hanging down limply, a synonym for sagging.

clue.text: Watch ever so unreliable, black inside

indicators.note: inside puts the single letter within the rearranged letters
unreliable suggests not in the right order, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A wristwatch that keeps poor time, with a black face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreliable' rearranges EVER SO into OSERVE, and 'inside' puts B within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to look at closely, so watch is a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Rag: it's arranged for free

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A cheap newspaper is handed out without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin for without charge, so costing nothing.

clue.text: Boy catches some poetry

parts.note: nets means catches, as a verb

explanation.surface: A lad snaring some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets are fourteen-line poems, so examples of verse.

clue.text: One country or another welcoming almost everyone

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the shortened word goes inside the country
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: One nation or other opening its doors to nearly everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One country or another' reads as a single vague phrase, but 'One country' is the definition and 'another' is wordplay for a second nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a nation, the definition simply its category.

clue.text: Very pale, he's an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pallid man described as a bit of an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means the grey colour of ash, so drained of colour.

clue.text: Sucker will disbelieve the basic truth, last of all

indicators.note: last of all means the final letter of every one of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gullible person will reject the plain facts in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, so literally a creature that sucks.

clue.text: Evil is returning with nefarious leader

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the two-letter word is read backwards
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wickedness coming back with a villainous boss in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sin is wrongdoing, so evil in the noun sense.

clue.text: Type of diving ducks finally seen on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the island
finally means the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Waterfowl spotted on a tropical island, plunging underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba diving uses breathing apparatus underwater, a particular kind of diving.

clue.text: Insulin, say, moorhen might produce

indicators.note: might produce suggests the bird's letters could be made into something new

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a water bird secretes insulin.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is one example of a chemical messenger in the body, the 'say' marking the example.

clue.text: Not entirely laid back, bees uniquely busy

indicators.note: laid back means set backwards, so the run is read in reverse
not entirely means only part of the words is taken, a run from inside them

explanation.surface: Bees are unusually hard-working, never relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ESUNI in 'bees uniquely', read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use is occupied, as a phone line or toilet is busy.

clue.text: Christmas prize giver, heartless

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the central letter is removed

parts.note: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel Prizes

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted person handing out festive gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a word for the festive season, from French for Christmas.

clue.text: Wild animals: sharks, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals the answer sounds like a word for swindlers

explanation.surface: Wondering whether predatory fish count as wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheetahs are big cats, fast-running wild beasts of Africa.
